_about: Topic 51 summary page (replaces pt51-summary). Content = the topic-51 scripts (math_patches/_ai_vis_t51.py) and the Hebrew lessons (pt_src/seg1-seg5). Build: python3 summary_pages.py 51.
intro: The exam rewards **thinking before calculating**. Six methods: **the math way**, **plugging in numbers**, **plugging in the answers**, **understanding**, **estimation** and **insight**. At home, solve every question both ways.

sections.title: The six methods: which one, when

head: Method
When do I use it?
How
The trap
rows: **The math way**
Always possible: the school way, with algebra, an equation or a formula
Solve it fully; at home, solve every question this way too
A long calculation when a shortcut was waiting
**Plugging in numbers**
Letters in the question and letters in the choices; an expression "$=?$" with number choices; ratios; more letters than equations
Pick an easy number that fits every condition, say why first; work out the question, then every choice; rule out three
0 and 1 often make choices tie: then pick another number
**Plugging in the answers**
The question asks for one number, the choices are plain numbers, and each one is easy to check
Cross out choices that make no sense; start with a round choice, or the middle one when they are in order; check it against EVERY given
A choice that fits only one given
**Understanding**
Must / could / cannot be true; signs; which is bigger; even and odd; order; the last digit
Reason with a rule you already know (different signs give a negative, $2k$ is even), without calculating
Use only a rule that is always true; not sure? plug in numbers
**Estimation**
The choices are far apart; areas, volumes, roots and $\pi$; a long calculation
Round numbers you know ($\pi$ is a bit more than $3$, $\sqrt{50}$ is a bit more than $7$); a range the answer must be in
Choices that are close: an estimate can't split them
**Insight**
The numbers look chosen on purpose: repeats, double or half, shared parts, symmetry
Find the idea before calculating
Only practice builds it: solve many

head: Rule
Example
rows: Say which number and why, before using it
$x$ is a length: $x=2$, not $0$
The choices must come out different
$x=1$: $x^2, x^3$ both give $1$, so try $x=2$
Different letters get different numbers
Rule out three; two left? a tie-breaker number
don't recheck what is already out
Keep every condition of the question
a root, a figure, a positive integer
Percent: $100$ at the whole
you chose it, so you can change it
"Not always": one counterexample is enough; "always" is never proved by examples

blocks.text: **Plugging in the answers:** one choice is right, so it fits every given; a wrong choice breaks at least one. **Plugging in numbers:** the right expression is equal to the question for EVERY number, so it is equal for ours too; a choice that gives a different result is out. Two choices can match by chance, so we rule out three. It is a **safety net**.

items: Does it look too hard for its place in the section? Then there is a shortcut.
Can I plug in the answers, starting from a round one?
Is there a letter I can replace with a number?
How big must the answer be? Which choices are impossible?
Is part of it shared, symmetric, or not needed?
Stopping at the first choice that fits when you plugged in your OWN numbers: rule out three.
A plug-in number that breaks a condition of the question.
Estimating when the choices are close together.
Calculating the fourth choice after three are out.
